title: Preflight health check suite and rollback scenarios for runtime upgrades
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic, repeatable preflight ‘health check’ suite for runtime and model-serving upgrades that (1) exercises fast-paths and degradation paths, (2) runs a lightweight perf/regression analysis against baseline snapshots, and (3) produces a machine-readable pass/fail bundle that gates promotion or triggers automatic rollback.

Scope: This ticket covers the test definitions, runner orchestration (ephemeral clusters or canary nodes), evaluation metrics and thresholds, and the automation hooks for rollback. It does NOT include long-running large-scale perf runs (those are covered in ENG-14988) but must integrate their artifacts if present.

Acceptance criteria:
- A composable preflight suite that runs in ~10–15 minutes for a canary node set and completes with exit codes + JSON report.
- Checks included: API smoke (generate/chat/embeddings endpoints), KV cache correctness for continuation tokens, batching path sanity (synthetic high QPS), quantized model output parity on golden prompts, p50/p95 latency and token throughput measurements, and a small eval for hallucination/regression on ~120 prompts.
- Perf gate rules: p50 latency must not regress by >15% vs baseline; p95 must not regress by >10%; tokens/sec change must be within ±7%; any metric outside thresholds marks gate FAILED.
- Quality gate rules: BLEU/ROUGE-like scoring on golden prompt set must not fall below baseline by more than 2 points; hallucination rate increase >1.5x triggers FAILURE.
- An artifact bundle is produced on completion: report.json, traces.tar.gz (sampled tracer), and a link to the bench-run dashboard with raw metrics.
- Automated hook: If gate FAILS during an automated rollout, the control plane must mark the release as ‘blocked’ and trigger the documented rollback playbook (notification, scale-down of new nodes, reassign traffic to prior runtime).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Runtime test footprint must be lightweight to avoid cost explosion; we will rely on snapshot baselines for heavy perf comparisons. For edge cases where noise is high, use paired statistical tests (bootstrap) rather than absolute thresholds.
- For quantized-run parity we compare structured outputs (normalized tokens) rather than raw logits to reduce flaky diffs caused by stochastic sampling.
- We will prefer deterministic seeds for synthetic workloads; however, we allow a short warmup window to populate KV caches.

Implementation plan:
1) Define canonical test cases and golden prompt set in repo: runtime/preflight/gold_prompts.md (owner: @liam_o).
2) Implement lightweight runner (k8s Job) that spins up a 2-node canary pool using ephemeral node-pools with labels preflight=true.
3) Integrate k6-based synthetic load for batching and throughput sampling.
4) Wire perf baseline lookup: artifacts stored at s3://redwood-release-baselines/runtime-1.19/snapshot-2026-02-12.json.
5) Produce machine-readable output and upload to release artifacts; hook into release controller -> if status FAIL then execute rollback-playbook.sh.

Test infra and metrics:
- Use bench-harness v2 (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/2894) to collect per-token timings, sampler traces, and KV hit rates.
- Dashboards: preflight summary in Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/preflight/preflight-summary
- Alerting: on FAIL generate a PagerDuty incident with summary and link to artifacts.

Rollout & rollback behavior:
- Promotion policy integrates with rollout-gates: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic. Preflight is required before 1% promotion for non-patch runtime changes.
- If preflight fails after 1% promotion, automatic rollback for the cohort is allowed; for >10% a manual approver (on-call release owner) must review.

Open questions:
- Should we feature-flag preflight so teams can opt-out for emergency hotfixes? (PM feedback: prefer guardrails that allow explicit override with audit).
- How to handle non-deterministic eval tests (NLP metrics can be noisy) — suggested: accumulate moving baseline and require 3 consecutive passes when noise is high.

Docs and artifacts:
- Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Preflight+Health+Checks (living spec)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894 (runner implementation)
- Bench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/1021

Next steps for this ticket:
- Finalize golden prompt set and baseline snapshot reference (owner: @liam_o)
- Merge runner PR and add CI job that executes preflight in the release pipeline (owner: @asha)
